chapter: Benny Meroff and Chicago's jazz scene
title: A twelve-hour day of stage shows at the Granada and Marlboro
summary: Four or five shows daily, a new show and line of girls every week, alternating between two Marks Brothers theaters with Charlie Kaley's band.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Now, this with the band - you used to have to get there in the morning and---
Well, now, tell the day - how that day went ---
Well, we'd have to be there at about a quarter to eleven or before that - ten thirty and then we'd get through at eleven at night. So, you did a twelve hour sketch.
Was it four shows a day?
Four shows on regular days and five on Saturday and Sunday and this is unbelievable -- those shows lasted over an hour - our part of the show.
And, there used to be some rehearsal time in between right?
Well, when you're doing--- when we were doing one show, we were rehearsing for another one the following day. And, uh, I mean the following week. So, we--- if we had to do ---
The shows changed what--- every week---

Yes - a new show every week. And, uh, the only time--- now this is only two theaters you see. In other words, this is the Marks Brothers theaters; two Marks Brothers owned The Granada and The Marlboro Theaters and, so, they had another band called 'Charlie Kaley', who would be in our place the following week but every week, we'd have a different line of girls and a complete different show - all the great stars that you can think of. All the great moving stars and all the great comedians---
Did you move back and forth between the theaters or you just primarily stayed in one theater--
No, no. We stayed in one theater for a week---
Now, the new show would be in the next theater---
The following week - yeah - and everything went this way--- and, uh, ---
This way means back and forth---
